traceability.notes:
The story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION specifies an ESLint rule that validates @story file references for existence, correct .story.md extension, safe path resolution, project boundaries, configurability, performance (caching), and robust error handling. The current implementation provides the traceability/valid-story-reference rule plus supporting utilities and helpers that:
- Parse and recognize @story annotations in comments and extract file paths (REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION, building on 005.0's format validation). - Resolve relative and configured-directory paths from context.cwd or process.cwd, including ./ and bare-path variants, with configurable storyDirectories (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - Enforce the .story.md extension by default, with a requireStoryExtension option to relax the constraint when desired (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - Prevent unsafe absolute paths and directory traversal outside the project, and treat any out-of-project matches (even if they physically exist) as invalidPath errors (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - Check for file existence and distinguish between missing files (fileMissing) and filesystem errors (fileAccessError), while converting low-level fs exceptions into user-friendly diagnostics rather than allowing them to bubble up (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). - Cache file existence checks in a Map to avoid duplicate fs operations for the same path within a lint run, providing the performance optimization requested (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION).
The dedicated Jest test file tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts is explicitly tagged to support this story and its requirements, and it exercises all the acceptance criteria: positive and negative existence cases, extension validation, path traversal and absolute path rejection, configuration behaviors (storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension), project boundary enforcement, and multiple filesystem error scenarios. The focused test run of this file passes completely, and the broader test suite for the project also passes.
Given that the story definition has not changed from the previously assessed version and all corresponding implementation and tests remain present and passing, all acceptance criteria and enumerated requirements for 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION are satisfied. Therefore, this story is fully implemented.
